checks: Checked c7ae7f430666e631 §3, (7)–(8). Distinct deletion witnesses in a minimal infeasible family give the deletion-hull criterion, since the hull deleting w_i lies in C_i. Conversely the hull family is infeasible and every deletion is witnessed by the deleted point. For one hull, the empty-hull convention handles the singleton.

Read the exact frozen seed statement and verified the lattice sites and component ranks independently. In P_1 the forbidden midpoint pairs ab,ad,bd and eh have midpoints e,j,t,v. At most one of a,b,d and at most one of e,h can occur in an empty vertex set, giving the upper bound five via the finite-set witness lemma.

For W={a,e,j,t,v}, the plane y=0 exposes a noncollinear triangle and y=1 exposes the other two vertices. The omitted sites b,d,h are outside its hull by their z,y,x coordinates. Thus every W site is a vertex and the hull has no other P_1 site. The deletion-hull criterion gives the lower bound five.
The one-site component has Helly number one. Exact anchored-component additivity then gives six on P.
